item.title: Valley Regional-Old Lyme clinches CIAC football berth with 3rd straight Principal's Cup win over H-K
item.description: Charlie Zelek hoists The Principal's Cup after Valley Regional/Lyme-Old Lyme defeated Haddam-Killingworth 47-28 in Higganum on Tuesday, Nov. 24, 2026. (Bryant Carpenter/Hearst Connecticut Media) HIGGANUM - The postseason is coming to The Hill. Valley Regional/Lyme-Old Lyme clinched an unofficial CIAC Class S football playoff berth, and a home quarterfinal to boot, with a 47-28 victory Tuesday night over Haddam-Killingworth in the 47th edition of The Principal's Cup. The win marked Valley's third straight Cup win over its rival and sent the 7-3 Warriors back to the postseason for the first time since 2024. Haddam-Killingworth, which had to win to have any chance of qualifying, finished 6-4 and on the cusp of the playoffs for the fourth time in five years. Valley's quarterfinal opponent won't be known until the final regular season games are played on Thanksgiving. Of particular interest will be the Naugatuck Valley League game between Woodland and Seymour, both 6-3. On Tuesday night, the Warriors struck for touchdowns on each of their first two plays from scrimmage, both receivers screens from sophomore quarterback Max White to junior wide-out Charlie Zapatka. They scored on five consecutive possessions (save for taking a knee just before halftime) and built a 34-7 lead through three quarters. H-K, led by senior QB Tim Hickman, senior running back Kyle House and junior receiver Jonathan Slane, battled back to close to within two scores in a wild fourth quarter that saw the teams combine for five touchdowns and 34 points. H-K recovered an onside kick and cashed in with a touchdown. Within 34-21, the Cougars recovered a Valley fumble at their own 31 with 6:20 still on the clock, but their inability to capitalize on that turnover took crucial steam and time from the rally. Valley senior running back Patrick Lynch punched in his second 4-yard TD run of the night, and while Hickman answered with his third rushing score less than a minute remained by then and White drove a final dagger with a 44-yard post-onside burst. Valley now leads The Principal's Cup series 36-11. Valley won the last two editions on the last play of the game. There was Sam Zelek's 43-yard field goal for a 9-7 final in 2025 and Tommy Troy's 1-yard touchdown and for a 22-18 final in 2024. H-K's last win was 20-7 in 2023. This story will be updated. item.title: Celtics’ Paul George hits rare career milestone during blowout of Wizards
item.description: Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Celtics’ Paul George hits rare career milestone during blowout of Wizards appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coming off three consecutive disappointing defeats , the Boston Celtics showed some desperation in their return to action on Tuesday night against the Washington Wizards. Paul George , in particular, came to life after a few disappointing shooting performances in recent games. On Tuesday, George put up 28 points on the night on 11-of-19 shooting as the Celtics staved off a late charge from the Wizards to hold on for a 131-116 victory. He made six of his nine attempts from beyond the arc, and in so doing, he joined an uber-exclusive three-point shooting club. Having entered the night with 2,495 made three-pointers to his name, the Celtics veteran has now become the latest member of the 2,500 made threes club — becoming just the eighth player in NBA history to accomplish this feat, as per the official ClutchPoints account on X. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) With this three, Paul George has eclipsed 2,500 career three-pointers 🎯 He is just the 8th player in NBA History to achieve this milestone! pic.twitter.com/H5oCvuFcUk — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 25, 2026 George has been an elite marksman in the NBA for so long that it should not come as a surprise whatsoever that he’s rubbing elbows with some of the best shooters the league has ever seen. Included in the exclusive 2,500 made threes club are Stephen Curry, the all-time leader, James Harden, Ray Allen, Klay Thompson, Damian Lillard, LeBron James, and Reggie Miller. Now 36 years of age, George’s touch from beyond the arc remains as clean as ever. He entered play against the Wizards averaging 3.3 made triples through 14 games thus far this season while shooting the ball at a 40.7% clip from downtown. In a perfect marriage between system and skillset, George has found a new lease in life with the Celtics . His perimeter-oriented play style is perfect for a Boston team that loves hoisting up threes, and as long as George is in Beantown, he’ll be able to attempt and make threes to his heart’s content — improving his standing on the all-time threes leaderboard even further the deeper he gets into his career. item.title: Charley Hull, Atlanta Drive's WTGL debut included a lot of 'laughs'
item.description: PALM BEACH GARDENS — Atlanta Drive's Charley Hull stood in a bunker at SoFi Center holding a conversation with team owner Arthur Blank. Hull, whose team was making its WTGL debut about 30 minutes later, then grabbed her wedge, and as Blank was walking away, holed a 30-footer. Looking on and nodding with approval was Billy Horschel, a star on Atlanta's TGL team. For Hull — and Atlanta — that proved to be the highlight of the night. Even with Horschel and Justin Thomas, both part of Atlanta's championship winning team in TGL's inaugural season, lending support from the team owner's box, Boston Common Golf held on for an 8-3 victory Tuesday at SoFi Center. Boston Common had the advantage of playing its second WTGL match. "Obviously it wasn't the result that we wanted, but we had a great laugh," Hull said in perhaps the most upbeat post-game press conference ever held by a losing team. "It is a lot of fun. It's nice actually to be ... I know we're not on the golf course, but you're in the golf environment, and having a laugh." Hull, one of the marquee names playing in WTGL's first season, is considered the most popular active woman's golfer in Europe. The Englishwoman is No. 7 in the world, a three-time winner on the LPGA Tour and although she still is chasing her first major championship, she has five runner-ups in the tour's marquee events. She has played in eight Solheim Cups. Hull, 30, also this year checked off what she called a childhood dream, appearing in the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit edition. item.title: Raiders Urged to Add $120 Million WR as New Target for Fernando Mendoza
item.description: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk. Getty The Las Vegas Raiders could have a chance to give rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza a new target. The Raiders dived head-first into the Mendoza era after shipping quarterback Kirk Cousins back to the Minnesota Vikings. While Mendoza has shown promise through his first two games, the Raiders could have a chance to give even more help after the release of a proven NFL receiver who is looking for a fresh start. Raiders Named Landing Spot for Brandon Aiyuk The San Francisco 49ers just parted ways with Brandon Aiyuk, ending a long and drawn-out breakup that included a long injury absence and deteriorating relationship between the two sides. Aiyuk cleared waivers and hit free agency, where he could be a target for the Raiders. Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox named the Raiders among a handful of teams that could be interested in Aiyuk, noting that he could give some short-term help for the rookie Mendoza. “The Las Vegas Raiders probably won’t be pushing for the postseason over the final month of the season. They’ve lost seven of their last eight, and they’re rapidly falling behind in the AFC’s wild-card race,” Knox noted. “However, the rest of the season is all about developing quarterback and first overall pick Fernando Mendoza . Adding Aiyuk could help with that process and could potentially help Mendoza well beyond the current season.” Knox added that the Raiders have some weapons already, including tight end Brock Bowers and running back Ashton Jeanty, but could always use more help for the No. 1 overall pick. They could find it in Aiyuk, who once signed a $120 million contract with the 49ers, but could now come to them cheap. “Still, the Raiders could use help on the perimeter, and Aiyuk would be a terrific fit for their offense. Head coach Klint Kubiak was San Francisco’s passing game coordinator during Aiyuk’s career campaign in 2023,” Knox wrote. Raiders Might Face Tough Competition Knox suggested that several teams could be interested in Aiyuk, including a reunion with the Washington Commanders. Aiyuk’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, suggested that Aiyuk could lean on his existing relationships — which could help Kubiak and the Raiders. “That’s just my guess,” Rosenhaus said. “There’s a lot of that in the NFL; you see people connect the dots where they have history where there’s relationships. I don’t know where yet, but that’s just my assumption that something like that could happen — a former coach maybe a former player that he played with, somebody that knows him.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Raiders Urged to Add $120 Million WR as New Target for Fernando Mendoza appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Wild Would Be ‘Interested in a Nanosecond’ in Sidney Crosby
item.description: Sidney Crosby Wild Getty The Minnesota Wild would be “interested in a nanosecond” if Pittsburgh Penguins captain Sidney Crosby were made available in a trade. The Wild just missed out on their top free-agent center target, Dylan Larkin, so the team may turn their attention elsewhere ahead of the NHL trade deadline as they look to acquire a No. 1 or No. 2 center That could potentially be Crosby, who may be traded by the Penguins if he asks Pittsburgh GM Kyle Dubas for a trade in the final season of his contract with the Penguins, which is unlikely to make the playoffs. If that’s the case, then look for Minnesota to be interested in acquiring the superstar’s services. Wild Could Make Pitch for Sidney Crosby In a mailbag for The Athletic , Wild beat reporter Michael Russo said that if Crosby were made available by the Penguins, then Minnesota would be interested, and Crosby’s relationship with Wild GM Bill Guerin — who he won the Stanley Cup with in Pittsburgh in 2009 — could be a benefit to the Wild. “And Crosby? From the Rubber City to the Motor City Born in Akron, Ohio, in 1925, Ford was the granddaughter of Harvey Firestone, founder of the Firestone Tire and Rubber Co. She studied at Our Lady of the Elms High School in Akron before graduating from Vassar College in New York in 1946. She married William Clay Ford Sr. the following year. The couple initially settled in New Haven, Connecticut, before relocating to the Detroit area in 1952. For decades, Ford stood alongside her husband, often with their children, greeting players after games, according to her obituary by the NFL. Martha assumed control of the franchise following William Clay's death in March 2014. She was 88 at the time and became the fifth principal owner or ownership group to lead the franchise since its move to Detroit in 1934. Aaron Rodgers announced over the summer that the 2026 season would be his last, and it's possible he's already played his final NFL snap. The Steelers announced late Tuesday night that Rodgers will be inactive for Friday's game against the Broncos , naming Mason Rudolph their starter. The decision is not injury-related. Coach Mike McCarthy is benching Rodgers, despite the four-time MVP's pedigree and the Steelers' possession of the AFC's final playoff spot through 10 games. https://t.co/F2qo4OawcY — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) November 25, 2026 Here's what you need to know about the stunning move by the Steelers. But Rodgers has struggled and now Mike McCarthy is making a change. https://t.co/wPSeMX3lmq — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 25, 2026 The Steelers have struggled mightily on the offensive end in recent weeks, dropping from 6-2 to 6-4 after they were able to skate by behind a strong defense earlier in the season. Joe Burrow surpassed 220 yards before Rodgers even completed a pass against the Bengals on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 10, and Pittsburgh's offense was sluggish all day long as the Eagles snapped their seven-game losing streak with a win over the Steelers this past weekend. Given the short week, Rodgers' pedigree and his familiarity with McCarthy, however, a benching wasn't expected at this point. The Steelers are undoubtedly looking for a spark from Rudolph as they try to make one more push to win the AFC North, but Rodgers won't even serve as the backup on Friday, indicating he could be out of the team's plans entirely going forward.

item.title: Virginia Tech football: Benji Gosnell represents all the right things
item.description: BLACKSBURG, VA - OCTOBER 26: Virginia Tech Hokies tight end Benji Gosnell (82) catches a pass during a college football game between the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets and the Virginia Tech Hokies on October 26, 2024, at Lane Stadium in Blacksburg, VA.(Photo by Brian Bishop/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Virginia Tech tight end Benji Gosnell was once a four-star tight end prospect out of East Surry High School in Pilot Mountain, North Carolina. He had scholarship offers from everywhere, including Ohio State. He committed to the Buckeyes as a sophomore in high school. Gosnell’s family later moved to Southwestern Virginia, where he played his senior season at Carroll County High School. He also had a change of heart about college, backing off his pledge to Ohio State and later committing to Virginia Tech. He was essentially Brent Pry’s first recruiting win as head coach back in December 2021. Gosnell signed with the Hokies and enrolled in 2022. Unfortunately, he missed his freshman season while recovering from knee surgery — his second. In 2023, Gosnell quickly established himself, playing in all 13 games and making eight starts. In 2024, he started all 13 games for the Hokies at tight end and was beginning to look like a future NFL player. In 2025, Gosnell was named captain and was expected to be a primary piece in new offensive coordinator Philip Montgomery’s offense. Things didn’t go as planned. Pry was fired after three games and Montgomery was named interim coach. And his offense forgot tight ends existed. Last offseason, the Hokies hired James Franklin as head coach. His new offensive coordinator, Ty Howle, is arguably the best tight-end developer in college football. They were also bringing a couple of former Penn State tight ends, Luke Reynolds and Matt Henderson, with them. Instead of leaving for another opportunity, Gosnell did what is rare these days: he stuck it out in Blacksburg, knowing his role may change. Gosnell has played in every game this season, but has a career low of six receptions for 33 yards. He still plays a vital role as a blocker and he delivers when his number is called. But Gosnell’s role is even more important than what he does on the field. He remains a captain under Franklin. Even if his role changed for his final season, Gosnell remains the ultimate representative of Virginia Tech. A true culture-changing player. While his numbers may not be remembered years from now, his impact will. After last week’s loss at Miami, which dropped the Hokies to 6-5, the usually reserved Gosnell addressed his team. He told them that while losing to Miami hurt, losing to Virginia in the regular-season finale would hurt even more. It was a message his coaches and teammates appreciated. Gosnell also spoke to the media this week and said that while he’s dealt with adversity, he wouldn’t change a thing. Great stuff here from Benji Gosnell looking back on his time at Virginia Tech with nothing but love

item.title: Ex-Mets hurler signs with Yankees’ division rival
item.description: Ex- Mets pitcher Freddy Peralta has found a new home. And it’s with a division rival of the Yankees. Peralta and the Baltimore Orioles are in agreement on a five-year, $125 million contract, per ESPN’s Jeff Passan and Ken Rosenthal of Fox. Peralta, whom the Mets traded at the deadline, went 2-1 with a 2.95 ERA in five postseason appearances with the Tampa Bay Rays during their run to the World Series. He was named MVP of the ALCS against the Cleveland Guardians. An unrestricted free agent, he had been linked to teams like the Giants, Twins, White Sox and Padres, as well as potential returns to Tampa Bay and the Mets. item.title: ‘He Didn’t Wanna Miss (Patrick) Mahomes’ — NFL World Takes Notice As NBC Switches Cris Collinsworth’s SNF Assignment for Chiefs-Bills on Thanksgiving
item.description: ‘You Just Know He’s Punching Air,’ ‘Can’t Make It Up’ — NFL World Reacts to Cris Collinsworth ‘Going Dead Silent’ After Patrick Mahomes’ Mistakes The Thanksgiving slate of football has always been one of the biggest days on the NFL calendar. This season is no different, with three blockbuster matchups set for the day. The marquee matchup, of course, features one of the best modern rivalries in sports, writing its latest chapter as the Buffalo Bills take on the Kansas City Chiefs. With the magnitude of the game and major ramifications on the line, NBC decided to change Cris Collinsworth’s assignment and bring him on board for this game. Cris Collinsworth Draws Chiefs vs. Bills Assignment for NBC A former wide receiver with three Pro Bowl appearances to his credit, Collinsworth became one of the biggest names in the broadcasting business, with 17 Sports Emmy Awards to his name. As a result, it was understandable that the network wanted one of its best announcers working the Chiefs vs. Bills game. At 8-2 (Chiefs) and 9-1 (Bills), the two teams are near the top of the AFC pyramid, and this game could end up deciding the playoff seeding come January. Add in the history and the rivalry component between Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes, and it is shaping up to be a matchup for the ages. Fans, too, were quick to notice the change in assignments. “Boooo. Disrespectful to the Browns,” Big Cat of Barstool Sports remarked , as Collinsworth switched places with Jason Garrett for Sunday’s game between the Las Vegas Raiders and the Cleveland Browns. Podcaster Farzin Vousoughian noted , “Mike Tirico and Cris Collinsworth will announce the Chiefs-Bills game on Thanksgiving night on NBC. Collinsworth usually takes off for Thanksgiving, but he will be on the call this year and will take this Sunday night off instead. In other words, he didn’t wanna miss Mahomes vs. Allen.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor But for all of the great work that Collinsworth has done on the booth, fans have also accused him of playing favourites at times and going above and beyond for the players he likes. The biggest example of that has been Mahomes. “Makes sense,” Dallas Cowboys beat writer Tom Downey pointed out , before adding, “He’s gonna need time to recover from glazing Mahomes like he’s a honey-baked ham.” Sam Chimenti came to a similar conclusion , claiming, “You can never pull Collinsworth away from Mahomes lmao.” Wayne Pruski added , “Great. A love fest on Mahomes. Well, we can watch the game with the sound off, sorry sponsors!” It remains to be seen how the exact game plays out and which way Collinsworth leans. But with both teams coming in on dominant winning streaks, Week 12 promises to be worth the price of admission. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

If the season ended today, only one Big Ten team would make the playoffs — UCLA. UCLA would have a road matchup against No. 8 Wake Forest. UCLA dropped from No. 4 to No. 9 after losing to Michigan last Saturday, while Indiana dropped from No. 8 to No. 14 after losing to Washington. Iowa rose from No. 15 to No. 13, Oregon from No. 13 to No. 12, and USC from No. 18 to No. 15. Oregon has the best Big Ten betting odds of winning the national championship at +2000, per FanDuel Sportsbook . Despite being ranked No. 9 currently, UCLA has +15000 odds of winning it all. The pessimism surrounding UCLA has everything to do with quarterback Ty Dieffenbach’s injury status and whether he’ll be able to play on Saturday versus USC. Dieffenbach injured his hip against Michigan but practiced on Tuesday and hasn’t been ruled out for the USC game. Per ESPN’s College Football Power Index , only two Big Ten teams have over a 50% chance of making the playoffs. ESPN’s FPI gives Oregon a 66.4% chance of making the playoffs and UCLA a 57.6% chance. With games beginning on Wednesday night, the Pittsburgh Steelers dropped a late-night bomb announcing a quarterback change. Veteran signal-caller Aaron Rodgers has been benched by the Steelers after a string of brutal offensive performances from the team. With Rodgers sidelined, the team will be turning to backup quarterback Mason Rudolph for Friday afternoon’s showdown against the Denver Broncos at Acrisure Stadium. item.title: Steelers bench Aaron Rodgers, name Mason Rudolph starting QB vs. Broncos
item.description: (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers have named Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback vs. the Denver Broncos in their Week 12 game on Black Friday, the team announced in a statement Tuesday night . The Steelers’ passing game took a massive step backward over the last two weeks, with Aaron Rodgers’ play actively hurting the offense. In that span, Rodgers ranks 26th in success rate and the Steelers have failed to score 20 points. On the season, Rodgers ranks 35th in EPA per play (min. 25 dropbacks). He has thrown 16 touchdowns to six interceptions. Rudolph’s last start came in 2025 against the Chicago Bears in relief of an injured Rodgers. Rudolph went 24-of-31 for 171 yards, a touchdown, and an interception in a 31-28 loss. He finished the game the previous week when Rodgers broke his wrist, throwing a touchdown in a 34-12 win over the Bengals. Let us know what you think in the comments . item.title: BREAKING: Mason Rudolph to Replace Aaron Rodgers as Steelers Quarterback
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterbacks Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph at practice on Sept. 11, 2025. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now The Pittsburgh Steelers have declared that Aaron Rodgers will be inactive for the team’s Week 12 home game against the Denver Broncos on Friday, and announced that Mason Rudolph will be the team’s starting quarterback. The announcement came via a statement from Steelers spokesman Burt Lauten after 11 p.m. on Tuesday, and did not include any context or reasoning for the change. Team sources indicated that it was a coach’s decision. Head coach Mike McCarthy had said definitively during his press conference on Monday that Rodgers would remain his starting quarterback. “Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback,” McCarthy said. Rodgers had his normal media availability after practice on Tuesday, and did not give any inclination that anything was amiss. “It’s November into December football,” he said. “You’ve got to be playing your best ball this time of year, so we’ve got to bounce back accordingly this week.” Rodgers and the rest of the Pittsburgh passing offense have been struggling. He has thrown for only 370 yards over the last two games combined. Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph during a preseason game on Aug. 21, 2026. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Rudolph, 31, has dressed as the Steelers backup all season. He last appeared as a starter in 2025, when he made one appearance in place of an injured Rodgers. In 2024, he started five games for the Tennessee Titans. In five games with the Titans in 2024, Rudolph threw for 1,530 yards, nine touchdowns and nine interceptions, while maintaining an 80.1 passer rating. He lost his lone start with the Steelers in 2025. IPL 2027 mini-auction: Full list of overseas players registered in Indian Premier League mini-auction with base prices and countries A long list of overseas players has put their names forward for the IPL 2027 mini-auction, and the full register offers an early look at who could be available when the bidding begins in Goa. The event is scheduled for Wednesday, December 16, 2026, with the action starting at 11:00 AM IST. The most prominent name on the register is Ben Stokes, the 35-year-old England all-rounder who retired from international cricket earlier this year. He has signed up at the top base price of ₹2 crore, and his presence is a boost for an auction that does not carry many marquee names. Some franchises may also see him as a possible captaincy option, particularly those that are searching for a new leader. In total, 1,220 players have registered, made up of 939 Indians and 281 overseas players, and they will compete for a maximum of 66 places across the ten teams. Only 25 of those places are open to overseas players, so the competition among the foreign names will be fierce. The initial list will be pruned further before the final auction pool is released. The register also includes 12 players from Bangladesh, which has come as a surprise in light of last year's controversy. However, Shakib Al Hasan and Mustafizur Rahman do not appear on the list, and their absence has drawn almost as much attention as the names that are present. The overseas group of 281 consists of 170 capped internationals, 69 uncapped overseas players and 42 players from Associate nations. item.title: Travis Kelce receives ultimate GOAT recognition from Bills head coach before Thanksgiving clash
item.description: Photo by Amy Kontras/Getty Images Travis Kelce has received a major endorsement from Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady, who has named the Kansas City Chiefs star the greatest tight end in NFL history ahead of their Thanksgiving showdown. The 37-year-old is enjoying another productive season with the Chiefs, having spent his entire 14-year NFL career in Kansas City. Kelce is coming off an impressive performance against the Arizona Cardinals, recording six receptions for 72 yards and two touchdowns in a dominant 34-7 victory. Joe Brady explains why Travis Kelce is the greatest tight end ever Brady was asked about the challenge of preparing for Kelce ahead of the Bills’ meeting with Kansas City and made his feelings clear. According to reporter Jon Scott, Brady called Kelce the greatest tight end of all time and praised the impact he has had on the position. “Joe Brady calls Travis Kelce the greatest tight end of all time, adding he revolutionized the position,” Scott reported. It is a significant compliment coming from a coach preparing to face Kelce in one of the biggest games of the Chiefs’ regular season. The veteran tight end has continued to produce despite being 37, adding another impressive display against Arizona to his already remarkable career. Kelce has also climbed the NFL’s all-time touchdown rankings. He now has 110 career touchdowns, including the playoffs, placing him third among all players in the position. Kansas City will need another strong performance from him against Buffalo, particularly with the Bills currently holding the best record in the AFC. The Chiefs enter the contest at 8-2 and sit second in the AFC West behind the Denver Broncos. A victory would give them a major opportunity to strengthen their position in the conference standings. However, Brady’s Bills will be determined to protect their place at the top of the AFC. With Kelce continuing to play an important role in Andy Reid’s offence, Buffalo will have to find a way to limit one of the greatest tight ends the league has seen. item.title: FSU men's basketball wins fourth straight, beats UNC Asheville, 97-61
item.description: Behind Sebastian Rancik's 22 points, Florida State men's basketball beat UNC Asheville 97-61 for the Seminoles' fourth consecutive win on Tuesday, Nov. 11, at the Donald L. Tucker Civic Center. It's Rancik's fourth game this season with 20 or more points, and his second in a row. The Seminoles shot 55.4% from the field and scored 46 points in the paint, utilizing a significant size advantage over UNC Asheville. After a cold stretch shooting from deep, FSU shot 42.1% from three, its best mark since shooting 42.9% from behind the arc against Ball State, and the eight makes are tied for the most this season, joining the season-opening win over FAMU. It was of a piece with their performance for most of a familiarly frustrating night that at least concluded with a shot of energy, the home side belatedly shaking off their torpor and ending the prospect of a triumphant return to the Etihad for Kevin De Bruyne. Despite the relief sparked by a fine equaliser by Rayan Cherki, who was rewarded for an insistent but hitherto fruitless evening’s endeavours when his angled shot flashed past Vanja Milinkovic-Savic, it was hard to see this as anything but a perfect snapshot of their autumn difficulties. Nobody could pretend City were up against crack opposition in a one-paced Napoli, who are eighth in Serie A and lack the brio of old, but they simply cannot keep the door shut and could not have quibbled about departing with a defeat. item.title: Dortmund’s Beier halts Arsenal charge after thunderbolt from Gyökeres
item.description: Arsenal’s sky-high standards are slipping. For the second time in four days, Mikel Arteta’s side found themselves a goal up at half-time and apparently coasting toward victory, only for their opponents to rouse themselves and earn a deserved draw. After Newcastle on Saturday , this time it was an impressive Borussia Dortmund who became only the second side to take points off Arsenal in their past 15 group stage games in this competition. It could have been worse had an offside flag not ruled out Jobe ­Bellingham’s goal after Max Beier equalised a thunderbolt from Viktor Gyökeres. But the much-maligned Sweden striker was guilty of a glaring miss late on as Arsenal laid siege to Dortmund’s goal, racking up 30 shots by the final whistle. The German side had to hang on for a result that gave their travelling fans a night to remember, although Arteta admitted his players must be more clinical when Real Madrid and Jude Bellingham visit north London in a fortnight. item.description: It was a record-breaking occasion in more ways than one. item.title: Madness erupts as Sevilla deny Betis in wild end to Spain’s ‘derby of derbies’
item.description: Rivals have been heading in opposite directions in recent years but latest clash showed some things never change “If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, this was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes past 8pm on Saturday evening in the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, it felt like there was. Frankly it was a bit rubbish, as bad a goal as you’ll see, but it was also the best, practically Pelé against the Nazis . Suddenly there were arms and legs everywhere, tears too. Cameras confirmed it. Zoom in and there they are: actual, real life tears. In the 91st minute of the 146th meeting between Sevilla Fútbol Club and Real Betis Balompié – “derby of derbies” according to Luis García, the Sevilla coach for whom it was the first – Salas’s shot from 18 yards went through Marc Bartra’s legs and Álvaro Valles’s hands. The ball dribbled into the Betis net so apologetically it barely touched the net at all and hadn’t got there before Sevilla’s vice-captain was gone. Raised in Morón de la Frontera, to the south of a city divided , Salas joined Sevilla at 11; now, having levelled the game at 1-1, he went tearing towards the terraces, absolutely losing it like they were. item.title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoided Sign up for our free newsletter here In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter. Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0 . Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023 . Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Neville, Keane and Manchester United meltdowns at world’s funniest comedy club
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Hoo-boy. Short of forgetting to put on his washable virgin wool navy trousers before striding towards the visitors’ dugout at Anfield, it’s difficult to imagine how Mauricio Pochettino’s spell in charge of Manchester United could have got off to a more humiliating start. Having witnessed his new team go a man and two goals down in less time than it takes to listen to Led Zeppelin’s Stairway to Heaven twice, it was a rendition of Sacked In The Morning that could be heard from the home fans inside 15 minutes. Poch would later complain that the decision to dismiss Leny Yoro was questionable, but it was far less baffling than his own call to hand Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in a year after almost 12 months out with knack. Across 90 harrowing minutes, the Dutch defender didn’t so much look off the pace as resemble a confused tourist who’d wandered on to the pitch while trying to find his way to the stadium museum. In a footballing world obsessed with micro-marginal-gains – think custom-weighted laces, aerodynamic socks, or nice calming shades of green for training ground walls – how about one modest proposal that otherwise does my nut in? That a multimillion pound player, paid hundred of thousands each week, has to walk all the way around the pitch with ligament injuries . Carry him, give him crutches, or put him in a wheelchair! Is it just me? It has a very 1950s amateur air of ‘dont make a fuss, ‘tis a mere scratch’” – John Williams. Since he was such a good friend to Mauricio Pochettino in his previous role, can we assume Donald Trump will be ringing the FA to overturn Lenny Yoro’s red card once he’s finished his morning nap?” – Declan Hackett. If Mikel Arteta is correct in his assertion that “ We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League ” how does he explain his team’s Micky Mouse defending for Newcastle’s second goal at St James’ Park on Sunday?” – Dominic Hodgson. item.title: César Azpilicueta: ‘At Chelsea a draw was a catastrophe – if you can’t perform, you’re out’
item.description: Former defender reflects on his record-breaking longevity, kicking Eden Hazard in training, and life after retirement César Azpilicueta looks well. César Azpilicueta always looks well – “ah, Captain Handsome,” one Chelsea fan says when told who’s turning up – but today especially, smiling in the sunshine. Strolling in, he eases into an easier chair, golf course spreading out beyond the terrace, west of Madrid, and orders a detox almost as green. It is nearly 20 years since he played his first game and a few months since he played his last, training kit replaced by bermudas, loafers and a polo, a picture of relaxation. So what’s it like not being a footballer? “Well, different,” he says. Then he laughs, which he does a lot. It is not a laugh-your-head-off laugh, more a chuckle, a giggle, as if amused at everything he did. And for all the self-deprecation, the lack of triumphalism, he did everything. Now, at 37, it’s not the same, although there remains much to do, Azpilicueta as understated and quietly busy as ever: “square,” he calls himself. He’s completed an MBA, a sports directorship diploma and there are media offers, a life to live. Matches to play still: against his kids the needle is never far away, he says. And although he hasn’t found a seven-a-side team yet he will. Continue reading...

item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

item.description: Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one. Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field. Continue reading...

item.title: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes
item.description: A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation “Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes. The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of Argentina’s football folklore are spliced with excellent archive material. Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. item.title: Ultimate 1-50: the male footballers best associated with each squad number
item.description: Who is football’s most legendary No 9? Has there ever been a legendary No 28? And why exactly does Mario Balotelli love wearing No 45 so much? Here’s our list and the stories behind it The relationship between players and numbers is a long-established one filled with memories and fascinating as well as fun stories behind them. With that in mind, the Guardian has had a go at deciding which male player is best associated with each squad number, from 1-50. Various factors were taken into consideration, including how long a player wore/has worn that number, what they achieved/have achieved in it, why they decided to wear it in the first place and, in some cases, how distinctly it has become associated with them in death. The below list is highly subjective and ultimately a bit of fun, but don’t let that stop you being shocked and furious in equal measure. *** Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
